glosses: To comport (oneself); to behave.

examples.text: Let an ambassador deport himself in the most graceful manner before a prince.

examples.text: Ask her to deport all illegals living in this town without a green card or the appropriate documents that prove their naturalized citizenship.

glosses: To delete.
To move from one place to another, especially to take away.

examples.text: He removed the marbles from the bag.
Thou ſhalt not remoue thy neghbours marke which they of olde tyme haue ſett in thyne enheritaunce that thou enheretteſt in the londe which the Lorde thy God geueth the to enioye it.

glosses: To move from one place to another, especially to take away.
To replace a dish within a course.

examples.text: But Richmond[…]appeared to lose himself in his own reflections. Some pickled crab, which he had not touched, had been removed with a damson pie; and his sister saw[…]that he had eaten no more than a spoonful of that either.

examples.text: The President removed many postmasters.

examples.text: This place should be at once both school and university, not needing a remove to any other house of scholarship.

examples.text: A supper brings up the rear, not forgetting the introductory luncheon, almost equalling in removes the dinner.

glosses: (at some public schools) A division of the school, especially the form prior to last

examples.text: A freeholder is but one remove from a legislator.
